content: This document provides a summary of information about the medication and does not include all possible details. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs. Warning: Mifepristone can cause pregnancy loss. Women of childbearing age must confirm they are not pregnant through a pregnancy test before starting this medication. They must also avoid becoming pregnant while taking this medication and for one month after stopping it. Discuss with your doctor the use of reliable non-hormonal birth control methods, such as condoms or a diaphragm with spermicide. If you become pregnant or suspect you might be pregnant, inform your doctor immediately. Uses: This medication is used to manage high blood sugar in individuals with Cushing's syndrome who have not responded to surgery or are unable to undergo surgery. Cushing's syndrome occurs when the body produces excessive cortisol, which can lead to glucose intolerance or type 2 diabetes. How to Use: Read the Medication Guide provided by your pharmacist before starting mifepristone and each time you get a refill. Take this medication orally with a meal as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. Swallow the tablets whole. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition, response to treatment, and any other medications you may be taking. Inform your doctor and pharmacist about all the products you use, including prescription drugs, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products. To minimize the risk of side effects, your doctor may start you on a low dose and gradually increase it. Use this medication regularly to gain the most benefit. Do not stop taking it unless instructed by your doctor. If the medication is stopped, you may need to restart at a lower dose and gradually increase it again. Avoid consuming grapefruit or grapefruit juice while using this medication unless your doctor or pharmacist advises otherwise, as grapefruit can increase the risk of side effects. Side Effects: Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, decreased appetite, dry mouth, fatigue, dizziness, headache, or joint/muscle pain. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks. This medication can cause low blood sugar (hypoglycemia). Symptoms of low blood sugar include sudden sweating, shaking, rapid heartbeat, hunger, blurred vision, dizziness, or tingling in the hands/feet. It is advisable to carry glucose tablets or gel to treat low blood sugar. If unavailable, quickly raise your blood sugar by consuming sugar, honey, candy, fruit juice, or non-diet soda. Inform your doctor immediately about the reaction and the use of this product. Symptoms of high blood sugar (hyperglycemia) include increased thirst or urination. If these symptoms occur, notify your doctor immediately. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before taking mifepristone, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This drug may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate dizziness. Do not drive, use machinery, or perform activities requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Mifepristone may cause a condition affecting the heart rhythm (QT prolongation). The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that may cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood may also increase your risk of QT prolongation. This risk may increase if you use certain drugs (such as diuretics or water pills) or have conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Mifepristone must not be used during pregnancy as it may cause pregnancy loss. If you become pregnant or suspect you might be pregnant, inform your doctor immediately. This medication passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/non-prescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Mifepristone can slow the removal of other medications from your body, which may affect how they work. Other medications can affect the removal of mifepristone from your body, which may impact its effectiveness. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss non-hormonal birth control methods with your doctor or pharmacist while using this medication. Beta-Blockers: Medications such as metoprolol, propranolol, or glaucoma eye drops like timolol may prevent the fast/pounding heartbeat typically felt when blood sugar levels drop too low (hypoglycemia). Many drugs can affect your blood sugar, making it harder to control. Before starting, stopping, or changing any medication, consult your doctor or pharmacist about how the medication may affect your blood sugar. Check your blood sugar regularly as directed and share the results with your doctor. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of high or low blood sugar. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911. Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Lab Tests: Regular lab and/or medical tests (such as potassium levels, thyroid function, blood pressure) should be conducted while taking this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose. Take your next dose at the regular time. Storage: Store at room temperature away from light and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Note: This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
